title: The Carpathian Castle
author: Jules Verne
short_summary: In the Transylvanian village of Werst, below a castle everyone believes to be abandoned, a shepherd sees smoke rising from a chimney that should be cold. Strange voices, a tolling bell and an invisible force drive back the two men who dare to climb up. Count Franz de Télek, who has never recovered from the death of the singer La Stilla, arrives and hears a voice he knows is hers — and the truth turns out to be stranger, and more modern, than any ghost.
extended_summary:
The shepherd Frik, looking through a pedlar's telescope, sees smoke coming from the chimney of the Carpathian castle, which has stood empty for years. The village of Werst is soon certain the place is occupied by the devil. Master Koltz the village judge cannot settle the matter; the forest ranger Nic Deck, engaged to Koltz's daughter Miriota, sets out to climb up to the castle with the cowardly Doctor Patak. A bell tolls, a voice warns them off, and when Nic Deck puts his hand on the gate he is flung to the ground by an invisible force.

Count Franz de Télek arrives at the inn and hears the story. Years earlier, in Naples, he had loved La Stilla, the great singer of the San Carlo theatre — and so had Baron Rodolphe de Gortz, who watched her from his box every night. She died on stage during her last performance, and Gortz blamed Franz. Now Franz hears her voice coming from the castle and sees her standing on the bastion, and he goes up alone.

He is captured. The explanation belongs to the physicist Orfanik: phonographs hidden in Gortz's box recorded the singer's voice night after night, including the final aria that her death interrupted; and a life-size portrait, lit strongly and reflected in angled mirrors, makes her appear as though alive. Gortz, discovered, destroys the castle and himself. Franz survives but loses his reason, and it is by listening to the recordings of Stilla's other songs that he slowly comes back to himself.

questions.prompt: What first makes the villagers of Werst certain that the empty castle is occupied again?

options: A shepherd sees smoke rising from its chimney
A light moves from window to window at night
A stranger is seen walking the road to the gate
The village dogs refuse to go near the hill

questions.explanation: Frik the shepherd borrows a pedlar's telescope and sees smoke where no fire should be. It is a beautifully ordinary clue — the whole terror of the book grows out of one chimney, which is exactly Verne's point about how superstition starts.

questions.prompt: Nic Deck and Doctor Patak climb up to the castle gate. What actually happens to Nic Deck when he touches it?

options: An invisible force hurls him to the ground
The gate swings open onto an empty courtyard
A trapdoor drops him into the moat below
A hand reaches out of the dark and holds him

questions.explanation: He is thrown down by an electric current fed from batteries in the laboratory inside — but nobody in Werst has any way of knowing that, so the story goes round the village as proof of the devil. Verne shows us the effect first and the cause three hundred pages later.

questions.prompt: The mysterious apparatus in the castle is the work of Baron de Gortz's companion, the physicist and inventor ___.
questions.explanation: Orfanik is the book's real engine: a brilliant, unloved inventor whose machines nobody would pay for, and who found one patron obsessive enough to fund him. Every 'supernatural' event in the novel is something he built.

questions.prompt: Where and how did La Stilla die?

options: On stage, during her last performance in Naples
In a carriage accident on the road to Naples
At the castle, years after she stopped singing
At sea, while travelling to meet Count Franz

questions.explanation: She collapsed during the final aria of her farewell performance at the San Carlo, with Gortz staring at her from his box as he had every night for years. Gortz then wrote to Franz accusing him of having killed her — the marriage was to have ended her career.

questions.prompt: Put the events of the mystery in the order they happen.

items: A shepherd spots smoke above the supposedly empty castle
The forest ranger is struck down at the castle gate
Count Franz arrives at the village inn and hears the story
Franz sees La Stilla standing on the castle bastion
Orfanik explains the phonographs and the mirrors
Baron de Gortz destroys the castle with himself inside

questions.explanation: Verne builds the book as a slow reveal: two thirds of it is village superstition, and only at the end does a captured engineer explain the machinery. Notice that the explanation comes before the castle is destroyed, so the reader knows the truth while Franz is still inside.

questions.prompt: Match each person in Werst to their part in the story.

right: The shepherd whose telescope starts the whole alarm
The village judge, who cannot settle the question
The forest ranger, engaged to the judge's daughter
The self-styled physician who is terrified on the path

questions.explanation: Verne spends a long time on Werst before he lets us near the castle, because the villagers are the experiment: each of them meets exactly the same facts and turns them into a devil. Patak, who claims to be a man of science, is the most frightened of all.

questions.prompt: Sort each statement by whether it is what the villagers believed or what was really happening.

options.label: The devil himself has moved into the castle
A spirit strikes down anyone who touches the gate
A dead singer haunts the castle bastion
A man is living there with an inventor
A current runs through the ironwork of the gate
A lit portrait is reflected in angled mirrors

questions.explanation: Each belief on the left has a machine on the right that produced it. That pairing is the book's argument: the villagers are not stupid, they simply live before the technology that would explain what they saw — which is why Verne set the story in his own century, not in the past.

questions.prompt: Franz sees La Stilla on the bastion and hears her singing. What is really producing the voice and the figure?

options: Recordings on phonographs, and a portrait reflected in mirrors
An actress hired by the baron and a hidden singer below
A painted screen lit from behind and a music box
A twin sister the baron has been keeping in the castle

questions.explanation: Orfanik had secretly installed phonographs in the baron's box at the theatre and recorded the singer night after night. The apparition is her life-size portrait, brilliantly lit and reflected off mirrors set at a calculated angle — an apparatus carried out onto the bastion in the dark.

questions.prompt: Baron de Gortz shuts himself in a castle so that he can listen to recordings of a dead singer every night, and refuses to let anyone else near them. Do you think this helped him live with his grief, or made it worse? Give your reasons.
questions.explanation: Both answers can earn full marks. A strong 'made it worse' answer notices that he stopped living entirely, turned on Franz, and finally destroyed himself and the castle. A strong 'helped him' answer might argue that the recordings were the only thing keeping him going, and that his collapse came when he thought he would lose them. Accept any answer that argues from what Gortz actually does in the book.

questions.prompt: Verne takes something that looks supernatural and reveals an invention behind it. Invent your own 'haunting' for a place near you: describe one thing people would see or hear, and the piece of equipment that would really be causing it.
questions.explanation: There is no single right answer. A strong answer gives both halves — a convincing eerie effect and a specific, physically plausible cause (a speaker, a projector, a mirror, a draught, a recording). An answer with only the spooky half, or with a cause that is itself magic, is weaker.

questions.prompt: The events take place around the Transylvanian village of ___, at the foot of the castle.
questions.explanation: Verne gives the village a full working life — a judge, an innkeeper, a ranger, a shepherd, a school — before anything strange happens in it. That is why the panic is convincing: we already know exactly who is panicking.

questions.prompt: Franz survives the destruction of the castle but loses his reason. What eventually brings him back to himself?

options: Listening to the recordings of La Stilla's other songs
Returning to Naples and the San Carlo theatre
A long sea voyage arranged by his servant Rotzko
Reading the letter Baron de Gortz had written him

questions.explanation: Orfanik hands over the remaining phonographs, and when Franz hears the singer's voice he begins to pay attention and gradually recovers. The same machine that was used to torment him is what heals him — Verne leaves the invention itself innocent, and blames only the use it was put to.
